tested_scope: At the exact pinned public commit, mechanically replay only the Redis branch of the detailed health endpoint under source defaults. No package installation, external service call, LLM/API call, hosted compute, optional monthly quota, protected-primary execution, or user execution is used. Database execution and whole-route startup are outside this slice.

observations.mechanical_replay: With REDIS_URL empty, health_details skips aioredis.from_url/ping and sets redis_status='not_configured'. Its final status expression returns 'ok' only when both db_status=='ok' and redis_status=='ok'; therefore even with db_status='ok', the source-default Redis branch deterministically yields overall status='degraded'.

exact_blocker_or_boundary: Redis is not contacted under the source-default empty REDIS_URL, so this slice has no Redis service/quota dependency. However, the detailed health contract treats intentional Redis non-configuration as degraded rather than healthy. Any parity route that requires a green detailed-health signal therefore cannot treat source-default zero-service operation as passing without changing that contract or supplying Redis. This is a distinct unresolved acceptance/health-semantic boundary and does not resolve the previously established missing-aiosqlite dependency blocker.
uncertainty: This slice does not execute FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, redis-py, the database dependency, or the whole application. It proves only the exact Redis/default health-status branch semantics at the pinned commit. Whether consumers require /health/details to be green is outside this tested scope.
